subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose a core `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` policy and own the associated timeout, fence, and shutdown lifecycle for third-party background context engines?
rationale: This is not a mechanical correctness choice: it establishes a new core configuration and lifecycle contract affecting plugin behavior, upgrade expectations, and same-session state ordering.

options.title: Adopt the core opt-in policy
options.body: Confirm that core owns the timeout and fencing contract, retaining the disabled-by-default setting and its compatibility documentation.

options.title: Move policy to an existing owner seam
options.body: Keep the liveness goal but place timeout selection and lifecycle policy in an established compaction or context-engine owner surface rather than adding a new core setting.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged until maintainers define a broader context-engine cancellation and shutdown contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the core opt-in policy
recommendation.body: Confirm that core owns the timeout and fencing contract, retaining the disabled-by-default setting and its compatibility documentation.
